question: Is nuclear power the best energy source?
analyzed_text: Absolutely. Nuclear power is the clear winner because it delivers what every serious energy system needs: reliability, scale, and clean electricity. If we want abundant power without carbon emissions, nuclear is the strongest tool we have. A single nuclear plant can generate massive amounts of electricity around the clock, in every season, in every kind of weather. That matters. Modern economies do not run on occasional power; they run on constant power. Nuclear provides that steady backbone while producing near-zero operational carbon emissions. The numbers are decisive. Nuclear power supplies about 10% of the world's electricity and nearly a quarter of low-carbon electricity globally. In the United States, it produces roughly half of all carbon-free electricity. And it does this using remarkably little land compared with sprawling energy systems that require vast space and major transmission buildouts. Nuclear is also one of the safest major energy sources ever deployed when measured by deaths per unit of electricity produced. It is engineered for precision, regulated intensely, and built to operate for decades. One plant can power millions of homes for 60 to 80 years.

verdict.summary: 2 of 3 checkable claims hold up. 1 has a wrong detail. 2 could not be checked against reliable sources.

claims.text: A single nuclear plant can generate massive amounts of electricity around the clock, in every season, in every kind of weather.
claims.verdict: Contradicted: detail (sources say severe weather events, including floods, winds, and wildfires, are a hazard to the safe operation of nuclear plants because such events can disable safety systems)
